title: Turn on automatic updates
why: Updates are mostly security fixes wearing a boring costume. The week a flaw becomes public is the week attackers start using it — updated devices are already patched.
action: Tonight: open your phone’s settings, find Software Update, and switch on “download and install automatically”.

title: Use a password manager
why: Nobody can memorise 60 strong, different passwords — so everybody reuses a few weak ones. A manager remembers the strong ones for you; you remember one master password.
action: Pick a reputable manager, then change your email password first — it’s the master key to everything else.

title: Switch on two-factor authentication (2FA)
why: A password can be guessed or leaked. A second factor — a code or approval on your phone — means a stolen password alone still isn’t enough to get in.
action: Enable 2FA on your email and social accounts today. Prefer an authenticator app over SMS codes when offered.

title: Back up the files you’d cry over
why: Phones get lost, laptops die, files get deleted. A backup turns a disaster into an inconvenience — but only if it exists before you need it.
action: Copy your most important folder to a cloud drive AND a USB stick today. Then open the cloud copy to prove it works.

title: Restart your router properly, monthly
why: Routers are small computers that run for months without a break; memory fills and small faults pile up. A monthly restart clears them and installs a fresh connection.
action: Unplug the router for 10 full seconds, plug it back in, and give it two minutes. Note the date — repeat monthly.

title: Slow down for urgent messages
why: Every scam shares one ingredient: hurry. “Act now”, “last chance”, “account closing” — urgency is manufactured to stop you checking.
action: Next urgent message you get: do nothing for 10 minutes, then verify through the official app or website — never the message’s own link.
